Staff Product Manager, Product Discovery Engine

Constructor powers product search and discovery for some of the largest retailers in the world. We serve billions of requests every week, and you’ve probably seen our results somewhere and used our product without knowing it.

We differentiate ourselves by focusing on metrics over features, and reinventing search and discovery from the ground up as a machine learning challenge with the specific goal of improving metrics like revenue. We’re approximately doubling year over year despite the market slowing down and have customers in every eCommerce vertical.

We’re a passionate team of technologists who love solving problems and want to make our customers’ and coworkers’ lives better. We value empathy, openness, curiosity, continuous improvement, and are excited by metrics that matter. We believe that empowering everyone in a company to do what they think is best can lead to great things.

We’re looking for a systems-minded Staff Product Manager to take Constructor’s search and discovery to the state of the art — and keep it there — across every retail industry we serve. This is a highly technical, high-leverage role at the core of our Product Discovery Engine chapter: the teams responsible for how we retrieve, understand, and rank the right products for every shopper, on every query, for every customer.
Your job is to raise discovery quality and, through it, our customers’ business metrics. You won’t be measured on features shipped — you’ll be measured on relevance and business outcomes, like conversion, revenue per visit, and search-attributed GMV, moving up.
You’ll start embedded with our Search Quality team, owning its strategy and roadmap and getting deep into the systems that decide what shoppers actually see. Over time, your mandate grows to setting direction for the entire Product Discovery Engine chapter — deciding where we’re heading and why across recall, ranking, query understanding, personalization, and the ML infrastructure underneath. This is a Staff role today with a clear path to Director as you take on chapter-wide leadership.
Search at Constructor is fundamentally a machine learning problem, so this role lives and breathes ML. You’ll partner closely with ML, data science, and engineering to turn the latest research into production wins, keep us ahead of both commercial competitors and academic state of the art, and be the connective tissue that aligns multiple teams — ML Recall, ML Infra, and, over time, teams like CORE, SABR, and Catalog Management — behind a single, coherent vision for great discovery.
If you’re excited about driving innovation across dozens of the world’s largest retailers, being held to relevance and business outcomes, and pushing an already best-in-class product further ahead, this role is for you.

Own business impact, not features. Drive measurable lift in search-attributed conversion, revenue per visit, and GMV alongside relevance across our customer base.
Deliver across every retail industry. Move quality and business metrics across all the verticals we serve, accounting for the differences in catalog, language, and shopper intent.
Keep us at the state of the art. Continuously translate the latest ML / IR research and competitive moves into production wins, and ship SOTA ML / LLM-assisted capabilities that beat our previous best on relevance.
Set chapter vision and strategy. Define the multi-quarter direction for the Product Discovery Engine — where we’re heading and why — tie it directly to customer business outcomes, and rally teams behind it.
Lead Search Quality first. Own its strategy and roadmap, driving measurable improvements in the relevance and correctness of results.
Orchestrate across the pipeline. Unify recall, ranking, query understanding, and personalization behind one definition of quality and one set of business metrics, so improvements compound instead of colliding.
Turn ML research into production wins. Partner deeply with ML and data science to take models — from candidate generation and recall to LLM-assisted interpretation — from idea to production, balancing accuracy, latency, and cost.
Make quality measurable and explainable. Build the metrics, evaluation frameworks, and tooling the whole chapter uses to measure, attribute, and explain discovery quality and its business impact.
Own quality under pressure. Lead investigation and triage when issues arise, and design durable, systemic fixes rather than one-off patches.
Grow the mandate. Expand into chapter-wide leadership spanning ML Recall, ML Infra, and — over time — teams like CORE, SABR, and Catalog Management.

* **Flexibilität, die zum Leben passt**

Revenue Growth Management (RGM) is one of The Coca-Cola Company's most important commercial capabilities, and not simply a pricing discipline. Coca-Cola positions RGM alongside brand building, innovation, and integrated execution as a core capability for topline growth, and our growth strategy names it a key commercial capability for determining where to play and how to win.
RGM connects consumer demand to the economics of the system. It determines what we sell, in which packages, at what price points, through which channels and customers, and with what promotional investment, all in service of balanced growth across transactions, volume, and price/mix.

Done well, it finds incremental revenue pools and converts them into commercial action, improves the economics of every price, pack, assortment, and promotion decision, builds the affordability and premiumization ladders that bring more consumers into the portfolio, and gives Coca-Cola and its bottlers a common fact base for growing customer revenue and profit rather than simply negotiating price.
We are now reimagining RGM for the agentic AI era, and we are building it ourselves.

Our Global RGM Product is evolving from a suite of analytical solutions into an intelligent decision platform where AI agents interact directly with enterprise data, invoke advanced analytics and optimization models, run and compare scenarios, and hand commercial teams a recommendation with the reasoning attached.

Work that once took an analyst a week (pulling the data, running the model, writing the story, defending the number) is being compressed into a conversation.
Few companies are attempting this at this scale, and fewer are still against decisions this consequential: real pricing, promotion, and portfolio moves, made across markets and bottlers. The work sits at the frontier of the CPG industry, spanning agent orchestration, retrieval over enterprise data, and the evaluation of non-deterministic and deterministic systems, and none of it is a research exercise. What we build ships to commercial teams who use it to make decisions the same week.
This is an opportunity to build, not just design, the next generation of commercial decision intelligence at Coca-Cola, and to establish the operating model for agentic RGM at global scale. The patterns set here will shape how one of the world's largest commercial systems makes its most important decisions. If you want your work in front of real users, at real scale, from the first release, this is that role.

As Product Manager, RGM, you will own the what and the why of the Global RGM product: which problems it solves, for whom, in what order, and how success is measured. You will work within a persistent, cross-functional product team alongside Data Science, Engineering, UX, Architecture, and RGM experts. Engineering owns how the product is built; you own everything that determines whether it is worth building.
Product direction starts in market. You will spend time with RGM teams at operating units and bottlers to understand how pricing, promotion, and portfolio decisions are actually made, where current ways of working break down, and which problems are worth solving next. You will convert that discovery into direction: clear problem statements, a prioritized roadmap, and requirements that tell the team not just what to build, but why it matters commercially.
Day to day, this is a product ownership seat. You will write user stories and acceptance criteria, prioritize the backlog against commercial value, define what 'good' looks like for each release, and sign off that what shipped does what the business needed.

It demands genuine fluency in what the product produces (elasticities, uplift against baseline, share math) and in the commercial world those recommendations land in.

You will stay engaged across the full product lifecycle, from discovery and pilot design through launch, adoption measurement, and continuous improvement - because adoption is the truest test of whether you defined the right product.
The role is global across a commercial system that spans more than 200 countries and territories, roughly 200 bottling partners, and 30 million retail customer outlets - few products anywhere offer a larger canvas. It is also a first seat: the product discipline you establish here becomes the pattern for how the Global RGM Product scales to every market.

s.h: What You Will Do for Us
s.t:
Own the product roadmap for the Global RGM suite: define the problems worth solving, sequence capabilities by commercial value, and present the roadmap and the value delivered to OU leadership and bottler executives.
Run continuous discovery with users: sit with RGM managers and walk a run end to end (which price moves to take, which to skip, and why) to understand where the product creates value and where it falls short.
Translate discovery into direction: turn user pain into written requirements with clear problem statements, examples, and acceptance criteria, and retest with the same users once a fix ships.
Write user stories the engineering team can build against, and represent the voice of OUs and bottlers in prioritization and roadmap decisions with the Global RGM Product Owner.
Own and prioritize the product backlog against commercial value, with the judgment to say no, sequence competing requests, and defend a prioritization call to senior stakeholders.
Define the success measures for each release, participate in backlog refinement and sprint reviews with the pod, and give business sign-off that shipped functionality does what the market actually needed.
Guard the product's credibility by catching recommendations that would not survive scrutiny in front of a bottler, before the bottler sees them.
Embed the closed-loop RGM workflow in the product (insight generation and opportunity sizing, strategy setting, guardrail definition, in-market execution, and post-implementation evaluation) so markets operate a consistent, repeatable process.
Design for governance: make RGM rules of engagement (price floors and ceilings, discount depth and promotion frequency, and price-gap and price-index thresholds) capabilities the product enforces rather than policies applied around it.
Support pilot design and test-and-learn discipline with market teams: hypothesis framing, control groups, and incrementality measurement.
Partner with the AI engineer on insight quality, rating generated insights and flagging output the underlying data does not support.
Partner with the UX designer on launch communication, naming, and demo material so each release lands with the business.
Build the business case for significant capability requests: size the commercial opportunity, weigh it against effort and alternatives, and make the call on what is worth building.
Lead each release to adoption: launch planning, capability building, and short playbooks (how to read an elasticity, when to trust a recommendation), with the goal of users opening the product without you.

# Product Manager Microsoft 365 Plattform & Digitale Zusammenarbeit (a) #
## 100% | Luzern | Homeoffice möglich ##
Microsoft 365 ist das digitale Rückgrat der Zusammenarbeit in der kantonalen Verwaltung und in den Schulen des Kantons Luzern. Wir bauen den Betrieb dieser Konzernplattform als eigene Organisation neu auf. Als Product Manager M365 verantwortest du, was auf dieser Plattform entsteht, in welcher Reihenfolge und mit welchem Nutzen für die Dienststellen und die Schulen.
Deine Aufgaben
* Du führst die Roadmap der M365-Plattform und priorisierst nach Wert und Risiko. Die Leitung sieht, was wann kommt, und kann steuern.
* Du baust den Zugang für die Dienststellen aus: eine Adresse für Anliegen, ein sichtbares Backlog, klare Zuständigkeit für jeden Entscheid. Kein Begehren versandet, keines geht an Entscheidungsgremien vorbei.
* Neue Dienste oder Apps bringst du zügig und nachweisbar zur Freigabe, gemeinsam mit Security, Datenschutz und den Fachverantwortlichen. Datenschutz ist für dich ein Qualitätsmerkmal und keine Bremse.
* Du machst transparent, was die Plattform und die einzelnen Dienste kosten, und legst sie verursachergerecht auf Verwaltung und Schulen um. Du unterstützt die Leitung bei der finanziellen Planung und Budgetierung.
* Du planst Rollouts mit Kommunikation und Befähigung und weist den Nutzen an Kennzahlen nach.
* Du baust das M365-Betriebsmodell mit auf, überführst Aufgaben vom externen Partner in die eigene Organisation und arbeitest im skalierten agilen Setup (SAFe) eng mit dem Product Owner, den DevOps Engineers, der Architektur und den Business Ownern zusammen.
Dein Profil
* Abgeschlossenes Studium oder gleichwertige Erfahrung in Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik oder Betriebswirtschaft mit ausgeprägtem IT-Bezug (HF, FH oder Universität).
* Mehrjährige Erfahrung als Product Manager, Product Owner oder Service Owner für eine Plattform mit vielen internen Kunden. Du hast eine Roadmap schon einmal gegen konkurrierende Interessen durchgesetzt.
* Substanz auf der Plattform: du beurteilst selbst, was ein Begehren technisch bedeutet. Teams-, Meeting- und App-Policies, Berechtigungs- und Sharing-Modell in SharePoint Online und OneDrive, Gastzugriffe und deren Lebenszyklus in Entra ID, Sensitivity Labels und Purview, Voraussetzungen für Copilot, Sicherheitsbaselines wie CIS Benchmark und Secure Score.
* Du merkst, wenn die Aussage eines Herstellers oder eines Partners nicht stimmt und kannst deinen Standpunkt technisch argumentieren.
* Verständnis moderner Betriebsmodelle: DevOps, Automatisierung, Configuration as Code und Auditierbarkeit im M365-Kontext.
* Erfahrung im skalierten agilen Umfeld (SAFe) mit Roadmap, Priorisierung, PI Planning und der Zusammenarbeit mit Business Ownern.
* Erfahrung in der öffentlichen Verwaltung oder einem regulierten Umfeld von Vorteil.
* Du wirkst ohne Weisungsbefugnis: du führst unterschiedliche Interessen zu tragfähigen Entscheiden und bleibst verbindlich.

**Product Manager/in** mit Verkauf \& Einkauf 90\-100 % (m/w/d)

Ob Sie bereits Branchenerfahrung mitbringen, spielt keine Rolle: Entscheidend sind für uns Ihr **Drive, Ihre Lernbereitschaft, Ihr Interesse an Produkten, Kunden und Märkten sowie Ihre Freude daran, gemeinsam mit anderen Lösungen zu finden.**.
### **Was ist Ihre Verantwortung?**
In dieser vielseitigen Position arbeiten Sie an der Schnittstelle von Product Management, Verkauf und Einkauf. Sie gestalten unser Sortiment aktiv mit, bringen Markt\- und Kundenbedürfnisse ein und unterstützen dabei, unsere Produkte laufend weiterzuentwickeln. Sie werden von einem erfahrenen Team begleitet und erhalten gleichzeitig Raum, eigene Ideen einzubringen.
* Sie sind mitverantwortlich für die Sortimentsgestaltung und \-optimierung, damit wir unseren Kunden passende und überzeugende Lösungen anbieten können.
* Sie analysieren Markt\- und Kundenbedürfnisse und bringen Ideen für neue Produkte, Anpassungen oder Verbesserungen ein.
* Sie arbeiten eng mit Verkauf, Marketing, Einkauf und Lager zusammen, damit Ideen auch in der Praxis sauber umgesetzt werden.
* Sie sind Ansprechperson für spezifische Kundenanfragen, erstellen Offerten und unterstützen bei der Beratung zu unserem Produktsortiment.
* Je nach Erfahrung und Einarbeitungsphase sind Sie auch direkt in die Kundenberatung eingebunden. Der telefonische Kundenkontakt hilft Ihnen, unsere Kunden, Produkte und Abläufe und praxisnah kennenzulernen.
* Sie pflegen den Kontakt zu Kunden und Lieferanten und bauen tragfähige Beziehungen auf.
### **Das bringen Sie mit**
* Eine kaufmännische Ausbildung oder eine vergleichbare Grundlage.
* Erste Berufserfahrung ist willkommen. Wichtig sind Motivation, Lernbereitschaft und der Wille, Verantwortung zu übernehmen.
* Wenn Sie bereits Erfahrung mitbringen, freuen wir uns über Ihr Wissen – ebenso wichtig ist uns aber, dass Sie offen bleiben, Neues lernen und bestehende Lösungen hinterfragen.
* Sie sind neugierig, denken mit und wollen verstehen, wie **Produkte, Kundenbedürfnisse, Verkauf und Einkauf zusammenhängen.**
* Sie arbeiten gerne im Team, sind zuverlässig und bringen eine gesunde Portion Eigeninitiative kommunizieren offen, klar und respektvoll.
* Sie gehen gerne auf Menschen zu und haben Freude am Kontakt mit Kunden und an Gartenthemen, Architektur oder technischen Produkten ist ein Plus.
* Sie verfügen über fliessende Deutschkenntnisse und **mittlere bis gute mündliche Französischkenntnisse (ab B1\)**.
### **Warum zu uns?**
* Sie erhalten eine vielseitige und selbständige Aufgabe mit Nähe zu Produkt, Markt, Verkauf und Einkauf.
* Sie werden von einem engagierten Team begleitet und können Verantwortung übernehmen.
* Wir bieten Ihnen ein dynamisches Umfeld mit flachen Hierarchien und kurzen Entscheidungswegen.
* Bei uns zählt nicht nur, was Sie schon können, sondern auch, was Sie lernen und bewegen wollen.
* Sie arbeiten in einem Unternehmen mit rund 50 Jahren Geschichte, das sich laufend weiterentwickelt.

The future of construction software isn't a single closed platform — it's a connected ecosystem. As our Technical Product Manager for Integrations, you'll own how Cosuno connects to the third-party systems our customers already rely on, from estimating and ERP tools like RIB iTWO to the open REST API that lets others build on top of us.

You'll be the bridge between our customers, our engineers, and our platform — turning real-world integration needs into a roadmap that makes Cosuno the infrastructure the construction industry plugs into.
This is a hands-on, customer-facing role in our Product team. Both our REST API and our connectors are still early, so you won't just maintain an integration surface — you'll shape it. You'll spend real time on-site with customers, understand how their systems actually work, and translate that into a product that lets them connect to Cosuno as seamlessly as possible.

s.h: In your first few months, you might
s.t:
Take ownership of our integrations product area — the REST API and our existing connectors to third-party systems such as RIB iTWO — and define where they go next.
Travel to customers across Germany to support them hands-on with implementing and setting up connectors, and to understand their systems, data flows, and constraints in the real world.
Sit down with customers to elicit integration requirements, then prioritize them against impact, effort, and our platform strategy.
Translate those requirements into clear, well-scoped tickets that our engineers can pick up and build — with the technical context they need to move fast.
Work through our API documentation and test endpoints yourself to validate what's possible, spot gaps, and represent the developer experience from the outside in.
Partner with Engineering, Customer Success, and Sales to make sure customers can connect their systems to Cosuno with as little friction as possible.
How we work
At Cosuno, we give people real ownership and trust them to do their best work. For this role, that means:
High autonomy, high impact: You'll own the integrations area end to end. No one will look over your shoulder, but you'll always have the support of the Product and Engineering teams when you need it.
Close to the customer: This is not a desk-only PM role. A meaningful part of your time is spent with customers on-site.
Technical by nature: You'll work directly with APIs, documentation, and connector behavior. You don't have to ship production code, but you do need to be comfortable in technical territory.
Platform thinking: We're building the infrastructure other construction tools and AI agents connect into. Every integration decision feeds that bigger picture.
AI-first: We use AI deeply in both our product and our daily work, and we want people who do the same.
Your profile

s.h: You'll be a great fit if you have
s.t:
3–5 years of experience in product management, ideally in B2B SaaS, platform, or developer-facing products.
Hands-on experience with APIs and integrations — you understand how REST APIs work, can read and reason about API documentation, and are comfortable validating endpoints (e.g. with tools like Postman) yourself.
A talent for working directly with customers: eliciting requirements, asking the right questions, and earning trust in technical conversations.
The ability to translate messy, real-world integration needs into prioritized, well-scoped tickets that engineers can act on.
Strong analytical thinking and a pragmatic instinct for turning complex problems into workable solutions.
Fluent German (this is a firm requirement — all of our customers are German construction companies and you'll work with them directly and on-site) and fluent English.
Willingness to travel regularly to customers within Germany.
